excerpt: ஆதாரமே நீ தான் என்று அறிந்த பின்னால்

sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
ஆதாரமே நீ தான் என்று அறிந்த பின்னால்
பாதார விந்தமே கதி என்று பஜித்து நின்றேன்
sections.translit:
AdhAramE nI dhAn endRu aRindha pinnAl
pAdhAra vindhamE gathi endRu bhajitthu nindREn
sections.en: After I realized that you are the foundation for everything in the universe, I started chanting your divine name and praying to your lotus feet that offer the ultimate shelter.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
நா அசைவும் நயன ஒளியும் நல்லோர் நினைவும்
மாவலியும் அம்பிகே உன் பிக்ஷை என்று உணர்ந்தேன்
sections.translit:
nA asaivum nayana oLiyum nallOr ninaivum
mAvaliyum ambikE un bikshai endRu uNarndhEn
sections.en: I have also learned that your alms include the movement of my tongue which leads to clarity in speech, the radiance and perfect vision of my eyes, aspirations to join virtuous company, and enormous strength.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
நிலவிலா வானும் அன்பனின் அளவிலா துயரும் சேர
செலவிலா நிதியம் ஒரு சேர்ந்தார்போல் ஒளியாய்
விதியினை மாற்றிட முழு மதியாய் உவகையொடு
உலா வந்த பதியின் இடம் அமர்ந்த திருக்கடையூர் தெய்வமே
sections.translit:
nilavilA vAnum anbanin aLavilA thuyarum sEra
selavilA nidhiyam oru sErnthArpOl oLiyAy
vidhiyinai mAtRida muzhu madhiyAy uvagaiyodu
ulA vandha pathiyin idam amarndha thirukkadaiyUr dheivamE
sections.en: Oh Devi, the presiding deity of Thirukkadaiyur, you are seated to the left of Lord Maheswara. You once joyfully moved across the sky like a radiant full moon to save the life of your devotee, Bhattar. On that new moon day, you appeared as though all unspent treasures of the world had gathered in one place. That day was one of unbearable suffering for your beloved devotee, yet your divine grace preserved his life. I have now come to realize your boundless compassion.

notes: The charanam of this song references the story of Abhirami Bhattar, a contemporary of Maratha King Sarfoji I (1675-1728). The Goddess, according to the hymn, threw one of her earrings into the sky and it shone like a moon to save her devotee Subramanian (his name was later changed to Abhirami Bhattar). If the moon had not appeared in the sky on that new moon day, the king would have ended Bhattar’s life for his erratic responses to his queries. As the legend goes, Bhattar was chanting Abhirami andhadhi over a fire during his punishment and when he was about to complete the 79th verse, Devi threw one of her earrings into the sky and it appeared as a dazzling moon. The king realized his mistake in punishing a saint and let him go. For details, see: Goddess Abhirami appears as radiant moon Abhirami andhadhi and Devi’s compassion
